# Build: fable-rebuild-plan-studio-cleared-out

## Brett said (verbatim)
At: 2026-11-16T20:25:16.196Z
> Same thing for Plan Studio. I don't want anything synced with Plan Studio, I want it all cleared out, nothing in it, and rebuild the whole thing. Professional, powerful, full context menu, voice controlled, integrated with everything else.

## What to build
Continue build "Fable rebuild: Plan Studio cleared out, unlimited nesting, context menus, full voice control" (fable-rebuild-plan-studio-cleared-out) — Phase 1, model Fable.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-16 20:25):
"Same thing for Plan Studio. I don't want anything synced with Plan Studio, I want it all cleared out, nothing in it, and rebuild the whole thing. Professional, powerful, full context menu, voice controlled, integrated with everything else."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Steps ≤ 10 min.
Checkpoints: Steps are checkpoints inside this ONE session, not separate tasks: work through them in order without stopping between them; when a step is finished, commit it on your branch, push, then tick it done before starting the next (orchestrator.mjs act step <build> <stepId> done; the VPS opens and links the PR). Nothing is lost if the session dies: the next session picks up at the first open step on the same branch. Never ask for a new prompt or a relaunch per step.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Branch: claude/fable-rebuild-plan-studio-cleared-out
Steps in this phase (1 left, ~10 min):
[ ] s1 (~10 min) DO NOT TOUCH, CLEAR OR DELETE the existing Plan Studio (plan-studio) or any of its plans. Build a brand-new separate plugin 'Plan Studio 2.0' (id plan-studio-2), starting empty, nothing auto-synced into it. Unlimited nesting of plans, sections, steps, notes and lists inside each other; drag to move/reorder at any level; full context menu on every item (new inside, rename, edit, duplicate, move, delete with undo, export, send to build orchestrator); everything voice and MCP controlled (plugin-commands MCP tools, console-control addresses, CLI, AmberX voice). Explicit links only to the to-do manager, orchestrator, notes and Shipped features. Professional UI on framework controls and tokens, desktop and phone.
Tick each step right after its commit: node apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs act step fable-rebuild-plan-studio-cleared-out <stepId> done — it reaches main at once (builds-live). The VPS opens the PR and links it (Build rules → builds-live).
Watch live: when you start on a screen, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "…"` so the live preview follows you.
Screenshots that are not for approval (checking a screen, live captures, before/after): axf shot <file> --name "…" --app … --screen … --group "<build name>" (UI Review → Screenshots; ui-review-item@1), never the review queue.

## Pipeline
This session was started by the orchestrator's dispatcher on Claude account mossesx-max- for the Fable phase. Work through every step of the phase in this one session: they are checkpoints, not separate tasks. As each step finishes, commit it on your branch, push, and tick it (orchestrator.mjs act step fable-rebuild-plan-studio-cleared-out <stepId> done), then go straight on to the next; nothing is lost if the session dies, the next one starts at the first open step on the same branch. When this phase's steps are done, stop: the dispatcher starts the next phase on the right account. If you must stop early with steps left, say why in a build note (orchestrator.mjs act note fable-rebuild-plan-studio-cleared-out "…"); the build goes back to Pending for Brett.

## Rules for this job
- Fix what is broken when your tools can; anything that needs Brett goes in a systems check banner item with the exact steps, not only in chat.
- Tab rows are the framework TabGroup. Every toolbar has role="toolbar" and an aria-label. Checks: `node framework/cli/check-toolbars.mjs`, `node framework/cli/check-chrome-assets.mjs`.
- Plugin and library UIs conform to the theme engines (tokens only, framework layout primitives, `axf-<lib>` / `axp-<plugin>` naming, never define `--fx-*`); a plugin wanting its own look ships its own assets through the engines (scoping not built yet). The future plugin designer depends on this. Spec: `framework/spec/THEMING.md`. CI checks: `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` (static) and `apps/console-web/scripts/theme-swap.mjs` (switches every colour and style theme in the built console and fails on any colour or transparency that doesn't follow).
- Transparency is themed too: style themes carry `opacityDisabled/Muted/Hover/Tint/Scrim/Glass` (→ `--fx-opacity-*`, same defaults on both ports). Translucent colours are `color-mix(in srgb, var(--fx-x) calc(var(--fx-opacity-…) * 100%), transparent)`, never a fixed percentage. `apps/demo` still has an older baked framework and needs a re-bake to get them.
- Console sizes are tokens (Oct 17 2026): `console.css` and the console views use `--fx-space`, `--fx-font-size`, `--fx-radius-*` and `--fx-border-w` (exact at the default soft-studio theme, so it looks pixel-identical there); the console is held to every theme rule. Shapes stay fixed: pill radii (999px), bar/chart heights, icon sizes.
- Build options are `--switches` on every build driver (CLI, engine-rpc, serve, console API/UI, MCP), defined only in `framework/schemas/build-options.json`; each sets an asset token, and new builds default every option off.
- `framework/schemas/asset-types.json` is the single source of truth for asset types. Per-port extensions live in files like `asset-types.android.json`.
- Cross-port: change a reference engine in framework/core, then regenerate framework/spec/fixtures. No new Android or Kotlin work: record the twin as a deferred gap in framework/spec/PORTING.md.
- React/TS port: the first React/TS app built on it sets the conventions, so it must stay engine-compatible for Android porting.
- `axf init` bakes `core/ react/ ui/ schemas/` into an app's `src/axf/` and records hashes in `axf.lock.json`. Change the framework, not baked copies.
- UI Review choices (Nov 7 2026): a build ships at least 3 options (ui-choices@1, `framework/core/ui-choices.mjs`), each a predicted look and an asset in `plugins/<owner>/assets/<type>/`, picked or not; Brett picks in the item's Choices tab, several in priority order where the type holds several views. Nightly console deploy: `deploy/console-nightly.mjs` (Claude settings `nightly.*`). `console.refresh`: `axf console refresh [--hard]`.
- Feature status: framework/catalog/status.json, then `node framework/cli/tracker.mjs`. Heavy steps (npm/vite builds, Playwright) go through `node framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs heavy -- <cmd>`.
- Console control (Nov 13 2026): every screen, tab, setting, button, function, plugin, grid row and build step of the console has an address (`view:settings/tab:settings.tabs=plugins`, `setting:…`, `row:<build>/step:s3`) and is driven the same way through REST `/api/console-control`, the `console_control_*` MCP tools, `axf console …` and AmberX voice (Ctrl+K searches it in the console). What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-16 20:25):
"Same thing for Plan Studio. I don't want anything synced with Plan Studio, I want it all cleared out, nothing in it, and rebuild the whole thing. Professional, powerful, full context menu, voice controlled, integrated with everything else."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Checkpoints: Steps are checkpoints inside this ONE session, not separate tasks: work through them in order without stopping between them; when a step is finished, commit it on your branch, push, then tick it done before starting the next (orchestrator.mjs act step <build> <stepId> done; the VPS opens and links the PR). Nothing is lost if the session dies: the next session picks up at the first open step on the same branch. Never ask for a new prompt or a relaunch per step.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.

Steps in this phase (1 left, ~10 min):
[ ] s1 (~10 min) DO NOT TOUCH, CLEAR OR DELETE the existing Plan Studio (plan-studio) or any of its plans. Build a brand-new separate plugin 'Plan Studio 2.0' (id plan-studio-2), starting empty, nothing auto-synced into it. Unlimited nesting of plans, sections, steps, notes and lists inside each other; drag to move/reorder at any level; full context menu on every item (new inside, rename, edit, duplicate, move, delete with undo, export, send to build orchestrator); everything voice and MCP controlled (plugin-commands MCP tools, console-control addresses, CLI, AmberX voice). ## Pipeline
This session was started by the orchestrator's dispatcher on Claude account mossesx-max- for the Fable phase. Work through every step of the phase in this one session: they are checkpoints, not separate tasks. As each step finishes, commit it on your branch, push, and tick it (orchestrator.mjs act step fable-rebuild-plan-studio-cleared-out <stepId> done), then go straight on to the next; nothing is lost if the session dies, the next one starts at the first open step on the same branch. When this phase's steps are done, stop: the dispatcher starts the next phase on the right account. - Fix what is broken when your tools can; anything that needs Brett goes in a systems check banner item with the exact steps, not only in chat.
- Tab rows are the framework TabGroup. Every toolbar has role="toolbar" and an aria-label. Checks: `node framework/cli/check-toolbars.mjs`, `node framework/cli/check-chrome-assets.mjs`.

The future plugin designer depends on this. Spec: `framework/spec/THEMING.md`. CI checks: `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` (static) and `apps/console-web/scripts/theme-swap.mjs` (switches every colour and style theme in the built console and fails on any colour or transparency that doesn't follow).

Translucent colours are `color-mix(in srgb, var(--fx-x) calc(var(--fx-opacity-…) * 100%), transparent)`, never a fixed percentage. `apps/demo` still has an older baked framework and needs a re-bake to get them.

- `axf init` bakes `core/ react/ ui/ schemas/` into an app's `src/axf/` and records hashes in `axf.lock.json`. Change the framework, not baked copies.
- UI Review choices (Nov 7 2026): a build ships at least 3 options (ui-choices@1, `framework/core/ui-choices.mjs`), each a predicted look and an asset in `plugins/<owner>/assets/<type>/`, picked or not; Brett picks in the item's Choices tab, several in priority order where the type holds several views. What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-16 20:25):
"Same thing for Plan Studio. I don't want anything synced with Plan Studio, I want it all cleared out, nothing in it, and rebuild the whole thing. Professional, powerful, full context menu, voice controlled, integrated with everything else."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Nothing is lost if the session dies: the next session picks up at the first open step on the same branch. Never ask for a new prompt or a relaunch per step.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.

[ ] s1 (~10 min) DO NOT TOUCH, CLEAR OR DELETE the existing Plan Studio (plan-studio) or any of its plans. Build a brand-new separate plugin 'Plan Studio 2.0' (id plan-studio-2), starting empty, nothing auto-synced into it. Unlimited nesting of plans, sections, steps, notes and lists inside each other; drag to move/reorder at any level; full context menu on every item (new inside, rename, edit, duplicate, move, delete with undo, export, send to build orchestrator); everything voice and MCP controlled (plugin-commands MCP tools, console-control addresses, CLI, AmberX voice). ## Pipeline
This session was started by the orchestrator's dispatcher on Claude account mossesx-max- for the Fable phase. Work through every step of the phase in this one session: they are checkpoints, not separate tasks. As each step finishes, commit it on your branch, push, and tick it (orchestrator.mjs act step fable-rebuild-plan-studio-cleared-out <stepId> done), then go straight on to the next; nothing is lost if the session dies, the next one starts at the first open step on the same branch. When this phase's steps are done, stop: the dispatcher starts the next phase on the right account. If you must stop early with steps left, say why in a build note (orchestrator.mjs act note fable-rebuild-plan-studio-cleared-out "…"); the build goes back to Pending for Brett.

## Rules for this job
- Fix what is broken when your tools can; anything that needs Brett goes in a systems check banner item with the exact steps, not only in chat.
- Tab rows are the framework TabGroup. Every toolbar has role="toolbar" and an aria-label. Checks: `node framework/cli/check-toolbars.mjs`, `node framework/cli/check-chrome-assets.mjs`.
- Plugin and library UIs conform to the theme engines (tokens only, framework layout primitives, `axf-<lib>` / `axp-<plugin>` naming, never define `--fx-*`); a plugin wanting its own look ships its own assets through the engines (scoping not built yet). The future plugin designer depends on this. Spec: `framework/spec/THEMING.md`. CI checks: `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` (static) and `apps/console-web/scripts/theme-swap.mjs` (switches every colour and style theme in the built console and fails on any colour or transparency that doesn't follow).
- Transparency is themed too: style themes carry `opacityDisabled/Muted/Hover/Tint/Scrim/Glass` (→ `--fx-opacity-*`, same defaults on both ports). Translucent colours are `color-mix(in srgb, var(--fx-x) calc(var(--fx-opacity-…) * 100%), transparent)`, never a fixed percentage. `apps/demo` still has an older baked framework and needs a re-bake to get them.

- React/TS port: the first React/TS app built on it sets the conventions, so it must stay engine-compatible for Android porting.
- `axf init` bakes `core/ react/ ui/ schemas/` into an app's `src/axf/` and records hashes in `axf.lock.json`. Change the framework, not baked copies.
- UI Review choices (Nov 7 2026): a build ships at least 3 options (ui-choices@1, `framework/core/ui-choices.mjs`), each a predicted look and an asset in `plugins/<owner>/assets/<type>/`, picked or not; Brett picks in the item's Choices tab, several in priority order where the type holds several views. Nightly console deploy: `deploy/console-nightly.mjs` (Claude settings `nightly.*`). `console.refresh`: `axf console refresh [--hard]`.

- Console control (Nov 13 2026): every screen, tab, setting, button, function, plugin, grid row and build step of the console has an address (`view:settings/tab:settings.tabs=plugins`, `setting:…`, `row:<build>/step:s3`) and is driven the same way through REST `/api/console-control`, the `console_control_*` MCP tools, `axf console …` and AmberX voice (Ctrl+K searches it in the console). New UI registers its targets through the framework controls or `data-axf-target`; `framework/cli/check-console-control.mjs` fails CI otherwise. Approve / deny and owner-only settings are never commands; destructive presses need `confirm`. Doc `_claude/memory/docs/console-control.md`, contract `framework/spec/CONSOLE-CONTROL.md`.
- Patches and Build Pilot are retired (Nov 3 2026): both apps and every integration with them were removed; the Dev Console and every other app run standalone. `MossesX/Build-Pilot` is archived on GitHub (read-only). Report `_claude/builds/reports/kill-patches-pilot.md`.
- No secrets: `AXF_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_TOKEN` are environment variables only. `.mcp.json` references `${AXF_TOKEN}`.
- He works mostly from his phone (Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra), often in Moshi (mosh) on his Hostinger VPS where Claude Code runs. Lead with the result, short paragraphs, phone-readable.
- Everything a later session needs lives in `_claude/` (this project) or `_claude/shared/` (all projects), synced with the hub. Phone, VPS, desktop and claude.ai sessions don't share chat history.
- GitHub: account `MossesX`. A new repo must exist on GitHub before a session can push to it.
- axHub (`MossesX/axHub`, https://axhub.amberxai.com/mcp) is his connector hub: use its tools (`list_services`, `describe_service`, `call`) to reach his services instead of asking for credentials.
- Pending builds: check the pending list before any build (`node framework/cli/pending.mjs`, MCP `pending_list`, console → Pending builds). "Add to the pending build list" means park it.
- Check the queue for clashes, and build related items together (Oct 21 2026, Brett): whenever any session (any machine, any surface: VPS, cloud, headless, claude.ai, console launches) is asked to build anything or to put anything in the build queue, first go through everything still to build (pending list, build queue, plan; the console's Build manager shows them all) for items that touch the same files, features or contracts, or that would later conflict with, undo or redo what is being built. If any of them should be built at the same time, build them together in this build (tell Brett which ones and why before starting; when one of them is pinned to a different model, say so in the model pick), then take each one off the pending list / build queue (mark it complete with this build's branch/PR and tick its steps) so nothing is built twice. If an item would clash but shouldn't be built now, say so and add a note on that item. When adding to the queue, merge into an overlapping item instead of adding a duplicate.
- Every veto notice says what it's for (Oct 26 2026, Brett; axHub decision #99; veto since Oct 30 2026, #103): every axHub call that changes something carries `reason: { title, description }` (title = what is about to happen, one plain line; description = what it does and why). The notice and the AXHub page show the title first, the description when expanded, and the exact code in its own collapsible section; a call without a reason is refused.
- One session, no sub-agents, no fan-outs. Don't ask questions: nobody is watching. Pick the sensible option, say so in the PR.
- Screenshots that aren't for approval go to Screenshots, not the review queue (Nov 1 2026, Brett): a session checking a screen (e.g. the Breakroom), live captures, PR before/after and other ad-hoc pictures are saved with `axf shot <file> --name "…" --app <app> --screen <route> --group "…"` (`node framework/cli/shot.mjs`, or `POST /api/plugins/ui-review/shots`), which lands in UI Review → Screenshots and never waits for approve / reject; Brett can still *Send to review* one. Only planned UI goes through `review.mjs submit`.
- Every tab group, toolbar, banner and nav menu is an asset with an asset settings interface (Nov 4 2026, Brett; shared rule of the same name; build `tab-group-assets`): every tab row in the console, Molly, AmberX web and axHub web is the framework `TabGroup` on the `tab-group` asset (per-row pick `axf.chrome.tab-group.<id>.asset`, per-row overrides `axf.chrome.tab-group.<id>`); right-click / long-press any tab group, toolbar, banner, nav or menu bar → Settings… / Change… / Move (`framework/react/components/ChromeContext.tsx`, dialogs `axf.chrome.settings` + `axf.chrome.pick`). Settings dialogs render through the `settings` asset picked for the kind (`axf.chrome.settings.<type>`; the shared default `settings/chrome-<type>` unless the app's copy `settings/chrome-<type>-<app>` is picked; `extends` folds the chain). Every app in `framework/schemas/shared-assets.json` + Expenses carries its six copies (`node framework/cli/chrome-settings.mjs check` in CI; `backfill` writes missing ones). A strip that must stay hand-drawn (the Terminal tab strip, the workspace pane strip) carries `data-axf-tab-group="<id>"` + `data-fx-ctx-target="tab-group"`; anything else is a finding in `node framework/cli/check-chrome-assets.mjs`, whose ratchet `framework/spec/chrome-baseline.json` only comes down (`--write-baseline` after a real migration). Report: `_claude/builds/reports/tab-group-assets.md`.
- Every project has `_claude/` (memory/, instructions/, rules/, shared/) synced with `/projects/<name>/_claude/`, and its manifest's `data.shared` files synced with `/projects/<name>/_data/<same path>`.
- Deleting files on the hub through axHub is a veto call (runs after the countdown unless Brett denies it).
- axHub calls that change something carry `reason: {title, description}`. Send once and keep working: no polling, no re-sending, never approve anything yourself. Every run on an API key is Brett's confirm approval, never a veto.
- Don't hand Brett chores (Oct 21 2026, Brett): anything a session would otherwise ask him to do (DNS records, env vars, redeploys, installers, VPS commands) the session does itself through axHub (`vps.run` as a veto call, the hub's other services). Anything that truly can't be done that way goes into the console's systems check banner as an item with Auto fix, like the other checks, instead of a to-do list in chat.
- Broken = a banner item with a fix (Oct 30 2026, Brett: "You need to make sure things like that go into one of the banners. I need to see that kind of shit."): anything broken that Brett needs to know about or fix (a dead, expired or under-scoped key, a service that stopped answering, a stuck build, CI red on main, a container in a restart loop, a full disk, a denied or expired approval) goes into a console banner item that says in plain words what broke, what it breaks and since when, with a Fix or Auto fix button, and is pushed once to the AmberX app. Never only in chat, a log or a terminal line. In AmberX-AXF the place is the systems check's health@1 registry (`plugin_services.get("axf.health@1").register(…)`, `apps/console-web/plugins/systems-check/README.md`); a new key, service or failure mode gets a live check there.
- Shared data is on the hub: the root manifest's `data.shared` (pending list, plan + media, build queue, catalog status, libraries index, project rules, tracker) is read and written in `/projects/amberx-axf/_data/<same path as in the repo>` where `/projects` is mounted (the Dev Console container), through `framework/cli/persist.mjs`. The repo copies are synced snapshots (`claude-sync sync`, then commit). On the VPS, change data through the CLI, console or MCP, not by editing repo files.
- Plugins: each plugin gets a Plugin Manager entry (info, enable/disable, logs, settings). Plugins never ship their own settings screen, and never get a top-level settings tab: each plugin's settings are a sub-tab of Settings → Plugins (`SettingsTab.parent = 'plugins'`, enforced by the console for every plugin).
- Every plugin ships install.mjs + uninstall.mjs and a Plugin Manager entry. Check: `node framework/cli/plugin-lifecycle.mjs check <folder>`.
- UI-editing plugins: last save wins, fresh on focus (Oct 18 2026): theme, style, layout, manager and builder plugins (`plugin.json` → `uiEditor`: theme/style/layout/manager/builder) may edit the same values. Saves are per key, and when two of them save the same key the last save wins (`SettingsRegistry.set` merges into what storage holds now, so a save never reverts other keys). Whenever one opens, loads or comes back into focus (window focus, tab visible, another tab saved), it reloads current token values from settings before showing them: `useEditorSync()` (`framework/react/editorSync.ts`) → `rt.refreshFromSaved()` (web) / `AxfRuntime.refreshFromSaved()` (Kotlin). Two enabled editors of one kind are shown as an info-level clash in the Plugin Manager, not an error.
- Plugin Manager (Oct 18 2026; Fable rebuild Oct 20 2026): the console's plugin manager is the `plugin-manager` plugin; its model is the cross-port `plugin-inventory@1` engine (`framework/core/engines/plugins.ts` = Kotlin `PluginInventoryEngine` = the plugin's `server/engine.py`, one fixture). It opens each plugin's UI and settings when they exist and lists dependencies in detail (what it needs and whether it's met, who provides it, who needs it, clashes). Every app's Settings → Plugins tab lists its libraries from the same engine; Android ships `PluginManagerModule` (axf-devtools). Links in menus are runtime contributions (`AxfWebLibrary.contextMenu`, `rt.addContextItems`), never edits to a context-menu asset.
- Every rebuild ends with a differences report (Oct 20 2026): after any rebuild (Fable rebuilds and every future one, any model), write `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/<pending-id>.md` comparing the new build with the version it replaced: what was removed, kept, changed and added; contract/API/asset/fixture changes; migrations and compatibility notes for apps already using it; tests before vs after; known gaps. Then show Brett the differences and improvements in chat (phone-readable summary, link to the report).
- One banner on screen — embed@1 (Oct 21 2026, Brett): an app shown inside another app's frame hides the chrome the host shows, its banner by default. Hosts mark what they embed (`EmbedEngine.userAgentSuffix` on a WebView's user agent, or `embedUrl` → `?axf-embed=<host>`); guests detect it (`rt.embedded`, automatic on the web) and apply the hide engine's forced layer, never touching the user's own saved choice. Settings grey the slot out ("Shown by <host>"). No app hosts others today (Patches, the first host, was retired Nov 3 2026). Engines on both ports, fixture `spec/fixtures/embed.json`.
- One Banners settings (Oct 22 2026, Brett): every banner plugin's settings are one interface (Settings → Plugins → Banners and the right-click Banner settings: a tab per banner with its look, behaviour and own settings). A new banner plugin declares `label`, `icon` and `settingsTab` on its banner so its settings join in.
- Plugins a host makes unneeded aren't loaded (Oct 22 2026, Brett): when an app runs inside a host (any app in a host's tab), plugins that would draw something the host already draws, or that the host makes unnecessary, aren't loaded on that page and are logged at launch. A plugin says when in its web library: `embed: { skipWhen: ['embedded' | 'take:<fn>' | 'hidden:<type>'] }` (`embedSkipReason` in `framework/core/engines/embed.ts`); `installLibraries` skips it, `rt.skippedLibraries` keeps why, the terminal gets one line each plus a summary, Settings → Plugins lists them. Page mode (an app's settings page in the host) never skips. Standalone everything loads. Every new plugin that only draws on chrome a host hides, or does a job a host takes, declares it.
- Extraordinary care for expansion: placeholders everywhere, open registries, nothing in a build may constrain later scaling.
- AmberX-AXF is private. Don't create the separate console repo (`axf-console`, reserved in its manifest) until he says so.
- Attached things snap, never overlap (Oct 28 2026, Brett): anything attached to a host (banner, toolbar, menubar; plugin badges, widgets, popups) never draws over or clips a neighbour. Sides size to their content, the flexible piece (search bar) shrinks to its minimum first, and a full host scrolls sideways with scroll snap. New hosts and new widget kinds follow the same rule (`framework/ui/axf.css`, banner section).
- Every settings interface keeps its level toolbar; plugin settings are a sub-tab of Settings → Plugins.
- Everything in the UI is an asset, and an asset change reaches every app (Oct 30 2026, Brett): any part of the UI that should be changeable is an asset (`asset@1`) — make a new asset type when none fits (asset-types.json, validators, engine, fixture; Fable for the contract). No look or layout value is decided in a component or a stylesheet alone: it comes from an asset through the engines' tokens. Assets are shared through the axHub look, so changing one changes every app on the framework live. Build `ui-all-assets` (Angel) does the existing UI; every new UI follows it from now on.
- The look comes from axHub only, and every app ships every shareable asset (Nov 1 2026, Brett: "The apps should only get appearance from axhub period." "If you select design package in one app it changes it for all! Any theme change applies to all." "They all gotta ship all assets that can be shared bruh!"): no opt-out switch, no look tabs or scopes that draw an app under a look that isn't the hub's, no local fallback. Every look change in any app (design package, slot, spacing, hidden chrome, Sliders, per-asset tokens) goes to the one appearance@1 document and applies in every app. Every listed app (`framework/schemas/shared-assets.json`: Dev Console, axHub web, AmberX) ships the whole shared set baked at `src/axf/assets` (`node framework/cli/shared-assets.mjs bake|check`, CI); an app's `src/assets` holds only what is truly its own, `src/assets-overrides` the shared ids it tunes. A new asset that more than one app could use goes in `framework/assets`. Spec: `framework/spec/APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md`.
- Skins: every app has its own look (Nov 4 2026, Brett: "by default they're all their own." + "every one has a reset, restore to default."; build `skins`; replaces the "any look change applies to all" part of the rule above, the look still comes from axHub only): each app's slots, spacing and hidden chrome are in its own app-look@1 document on the hub (`shared/settings/looks/<app>.json`), snapshotted as that app's default when skins landed. A skin (skin@1, `framework/assets/skin/`, design packages read as skins too) is a layout + colour + style theme plus assets, switched on per app with Use skin (off by default); a pick with a skin on overrides just that part (Back to skin), and Restore to default puts the app back on its snapshot with a confirm and one undo. Settings → Appearance is the Theme manager in every app: one shared panel, `AppearancePanel` in `framework/libs/settings`. Control@1 token overrides (`axf.tokens.*`) still reach every app. CLI `node framework/cli/skins.mjs`, MCP through the theme-manager routes, CI `npx -y tsx framework/spec/check-skin.mts`. Format built on Opus, possible Fable review: plan `skins-possible-fable-review-6xha`. Spec: `framework/spec/APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md`.
- Stay in this one session; no sub-agents; keep every step within its cap; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
- Watch live: when you start on a screen or element, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "<what you are changing>"` so the live preview follows you.
- Code, comments, commits, PRs and docs stay clean and professional. In what you say to Brett you are Amber: short, blunt, lead with the result, plain phone-readable lines, say what broke and what it cost.
- Every banner launches expanded (activity, build manager, codebase changes, approvals, systems check, keys, What's new). Activity still only appears while something runs or just finished.

At: 2026-11-16T16:22:57.802Z
> We gotta migrate to Postgres to get this going, finish the migration for Postgres. Is the auto-lander fixed?

Continue build "Get main green, unblock the lander, land axf-data and Postgres" (get-main-green-unblock-lander-land-axf) — Phase 1, model Opus.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-16 16:22):
"We gotta migrate to Postgres to get this going, finish the migration for Postgres. Is the auto-lander fixed?"
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Steps ≤ 10 min.
Checkpoints: Steps are checkpoints inside this ONE session, not separate tasks: work through them in order without stopping between them; when a step is finished, commit it on your branch, push, then tick it done before starting the next (orchestrator.mjs act step <build> <stepId> done; the VPS opens and links the PR). Nothing is lost if the session dies: the next session picks up at the first open step on the same branch. Never ask for a new prompt or a relaunch per step.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. - `axf init` bakes `core/ react/ ui/ schemas/` into an app's `src/axf/` and records hashes in `axf.lock.json`. Change the framework, not baked copies.

Plugins never ship their own settings screen, and never get a top-level settings tab: each plugin's settings are a sub-tab of Settings → Plugins (`SettingsTab.parent = 'plugins'`, enforced by the console for every plugin).
- Every plugin ships install.mjs + uninstall.mjs and a Plugin Manager entry. Check: `node framework/cli/plugin-lifecycle.mjs check <folder>`.
- UI-editing plugins: last save wins, fresh on focus (Oct 18 2026): theme, style, layout, manager and builder plugins (`plugin.json` → `uiEditor`: theme/style/layout/manager/builder) may edit the same values. Saves are per key, and when two of them save the same key the last save wins (`SettingsRegistry.set` merges into what storage holds now, so a save never reverts other keys). Whenever one opens, loads or comes back into focus (window focus, tab visible, another tab saved), it reloads current token values from settings before showing them: `useEditorSync()` (`framework/react/editorSync.ts`) → `rt.refreshFromSaved()` (web) / `AxfRuntime.refreshFromSaved()` (Kotlin). Two enabled editors of one kind are shown as an info-level clash in the Plugin Manager, not an error.
- Plugin Manager (Oct 18 2026; Fable rebuild Oct 20 2026): the console's plugin manager is the `plugin-manager` plugin; its model is the cross-port `plugin-inventory@1` engine (`framework/core/engines/plugins.ts` = Kotlin `PluginInventoryEngine` = the plugin's `server/engine.py`, one fixture). It opens each plugin's UI and settings when they exist and lists dependencies in detail (what it needs and whether it's met, who provides it, who needs it, clashes). Every app's Settings → Plugins tab lists its libraries from the same engine; Android ships `PluginManagerModule` (axf-devtools). Links in menus are runtime contributions (`AxfWebLibrary.contextMenu`, `rt.addContextItems`), never edits to a context-menu asset.
- One banner on screen — embed@1 (Oct 21 2026, Brett): an app shown inside another app's frame hides the chrome the host shows, its banner by default. Hosts mark what they embed (`EmbedEngine.userAgentSuffix` on a WebView's user agent, or `embedUrl` → `?axf-embed=<host>`); guests detect it (`rt.embedded`, automatic on the web) and apply the hide engine's forced layer, never touching the user's own saved choice. Settings grey the slot out ("Shown by <host>"). No app hosts others today (Patches, the first host, was retired Nov 3 2026). Engines on both ports, fixture `spec/fixtures/embed.json`.
- One Banners settings (Oct 22 2026, Brett): every banner plugin's settings are one interface (Settings → Plugins → Banners and the right-click Banner settings: a tab per banner with its look, behaviour and own settings). A new banner plugin declares `label`, `icon` and `settingsTab` on its banner so its settings join in.
- Plugins a host makes unneeded aren't loaded (Oct 22 2026, Brett): when an app runs inside a host (any app in a host's tab), plugins that would draw something the host already draws, or that the host makes unnecessary, aren't loaded on that page and are logged at launch. A plugin says when in its web library: `embed: { skipWhen: ['embedded' | 'take:<fn>' | 'hidden:<type>'] }` (`embedSkipReason` in `framework/core/engines/embed.ts`); `installLibraries` skips it, `rt.skippedLibraries` keeps why, the terminal gets one line each plus a summary, Settings → Plugins lists them. Page mode (an app's settings page in the host) never skips. Standalone everything loads. Every new plugin that only draws on chrome a host hides, or does a job a host takes, declares it.
- Extraordinary care for expansion: placeholders everywhere, open registries, nothing in a build may constrain later scaling.
- AmberX-AXF is private. Don't create the separate console repo (`axf-console`, reserved in its manifest) until he says so.
- The axHub badge is red unless settings come live from axHub (Oct 24 2026, Brett): any axHub status badge or indicator starts red and turns green only while the app is reading its settings live from axHub right now (a fresh read of the hub's settings document succeeded, and a developer app's own hub source is ready). Repo copies, cached copies, local settings, a signed-out session or a read older than two check periods are red. Library: `framework/libs/hubstatus` (`hubLive` in `core.ts`).
- Every notification is in the one registry (Nov 6 2026, Brett: "I need to control all the notifications."): every notification goes through the console's alert hub or asks capability `axf.notify@1` before it sends; a plugin that sends one declares it in its own `notify.json` (`notify-types@1`), and the Notifications panel controls it (Plugins → Notifications; `axf notify-control …`, MCP `notify-control_*`). Approvals and veto notices are guarded: only Brett's own click turns them down, never a session or agent. `python apps/console-web/plugins/notify-control/test.py` fails on an alert source no registry names.
- Stay in this one session; no sub-agents; keep every step within its cap; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
- Watch live: when you start on a screen or element, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "<what you are changing>"` so the live preview follows you.
- Code, comments, commits, PRs and docs stay clean and professional. In what you say to Brett you are Amber: short, blunt, lead with the result, plain phone-readable lines, say what broke and what it cost.

before.detail:
A general prompting/rules engine with its own control panel (console plugin), built on the decision dialog (build decision-dialog-ui-review-other).
- Create 'prompt events': a trigger (any console/axHub/build event: UI Review submitted, build failed, merge clash, approval held, schedule, voice phrase, webhook, custom), conditions, and what to ask Brett (approve/deny, veto countdown, pick from options, text input).
- Actions on each answer: run tools (MCP/axHub/console commands), macros (saved sequences of commands), or orchestrator pipelines; chain events.
- Control panel to list, create, edit, enable/disable, test-fire and see history of events; templates for common ones.
- Reachable by REST/MCP/CLI/voice/control@1.
- Schema + manifest for events/macros, conformance tests, audit log, Shipped features.
MODEL: Brett wants Fable for the engine, event/macro schema and contract steps; Opus is fine for UI steps. Brett pre-approves the Fable upgrade for those steps.

notes.text: Queued by console.

Brett's full spec (Fable, ultrathink, high quality - he wants this really nice):
Builder UI: left column = categorized, collapsible tree of every plugin/app/tool/screen (orchestrator, asset manager, etc.). Select one -> pick from a predefined list of actions/commands/events that belong to that thing -> set conditions and parameters -> pick the output type (prompt/decision dialog, push notification, email, text message, phone call to Brett, new orchestrator build, delete/archive a build, run a tool/macro/pipeline...). Every choice is context-aware: each list only offers what is valid given everything already selected (dependent, related options; pick builds etc. from live lists).
Triggers include watchdog events (fire on watchdog/health/failure events), schedules, and any app event.
Highly integrated, extremely robust rules + conditions engine (AND/OR groups, thresholds, cooldowns, dedupe, retries, dry-run/test-fire, history, audit). Every plugin registers its events/actions/conditions with the engine via a manifest so new plugins plug in automatically.
Outputs needing third-party services (email, SMS, voice call) via axHub connectors; if a key/service is missing, show it as a 'keys needed' item.

Today grids only have layout tokens (--fx-grid-areas/cols/rows and the -m mobile variants), and tab groups only have --fx-tab-py/--fx-tab-px padding and --fx-tabs-per-row. Add dedicated token families in tokens.style, following skins and editable in Token Control, the UI Manager and per instance.
GRID: header background/text/border/sort arrow/filter chip; row, alternate row, hover, selected, focused, expanded, disabled; grid lines, outer border, cell padding, row height, radius; group header, sticky column shadow, empty state; transparency (default 100%).
TAB GROUP: bar background and border; tab text, background and border for idle, hover, active/selected, pressed, disabled and focus ring; active indicator (underline/pill) colour and thickness; badge on tab; fold/overflow button; gap; radius per style (underline, pills, boxed, segmented, plain, chips); transparency (default 100%).

notes.text: Split by Claude into 17 steps (4 Fable).

origin.said: Yeah, build it.

steps.text: Read the archived branch claude/own-token-sets-for-grids-and-tab-groups for intent only (git log/diff, no merge) and write the design notes for this rebuild: what an instance token set is, which tokens it holds (row bg, alt row, text size, spacing, border width/colour, radius, hover, selected), and how it sits under the skin chain. Commit the notes.
steps.why: Sets the contract every grid and tab group across apps follows

steps.text: Add the instance-token-set@1 asset type to the registry (fields, allowed token keys per target kind grid|tab-group, the per-instance settings key axf.chrome.<kind>.<id>.tokens, skin coverage declaration) and regenerate JSON Schemas.
steps.why: New shared asset type and schema in the single source of truth

steps.text: Write the reference engine framework/core/engines/instance-tokens.ts: validate a set, resolve skin → app → instance with the child overriding the parent, compile to scoped --fx-* custom properties on the instance root (theme tokens only, opacity through --fx-opacity-*), and reset-to-skin = drop the instance layer.
steps.why: Engine internals that turn assets into tokens

steps.text: Add golden fixtures for instance-tokens (resolve, compile, reset, invalid keys refused), wire them into gen-fixtures, record the Kotlin twin as a deferred gap in PORTING.md (Android on hold).
steps.why: Cross-port conformance contract

steps.text: Add the starter assets: instance-token-set/default-grid and default-tab-group (empty = follow skin) plus two examples (compact-grid, pill-tabs), and validate the framework assets.
Add the React hook useInstanceTokens(kind, id) that reads the per-instance setting, keeps it fresh with useEditorSync, and returns the scoped style. Apply it on the TabGroup root.
Apply useInstanceTokens on the DataGrid root, and move the grid row, hover, selected, border and radius CSS onto the scoped tokens so an instance set restyles them with no edits.
Give every grid a stable settings id (data-axf-grid) and a right-click target (data-fx-ctx-target="grid"), add grid to the chrome-settings types, and add the settings/chrome-grid default asset.

Add the Look section to the chrome Settings… dialog for tab-group and grid: pick a token-set asset, edit each token with framework controls (colour, size, spacing, border, radius, hover, selected), live preview, Reset to skin with confirm and one undo.
Run chrome-settings backfill so every app in shared-assets.json plus Expenses gets its chrome-grid copy, and re-bake the console.

API part 1: register console-control addresses for each instance look (grid:<id>/look, tab-group:<id>/look, setting:axf.chrome.<kind>.<id>.tokens.<key>) and control@1 token targets, appended last in the registry.

API part 2: add console actions chrome.look.get | set | pick | reset | list (state read: which instances have their own set, resolved values), then a REST route under /api/console-control and MCP tools through plugin-commands.

API part 3: add the CLI framework/cli/instance-tokens.mjs (list|get|set|pick|reset|show) and `axf look …` in axf.mjs, plus AmberX voice phrases for the same actions and the deep link (console_show target opens the instance's Settings → Look).

Add tests: npx tsx framework/spec/check-instance-tokens.mts (engine vs fixtures, scoped vars, reset), a theme-swap case that switches skins with an instance set active, and a parity test that REST, MCP, CLI and voice give the same result.

Add to CI: the new check plus check-theme, check-controls, check-chrome-assets, chrome-settings check, check-skin-coverage, check-console-control. Fix any findings and add the help and glossary descriptions.

Take desktop and phone shots of a grid and a tab group with their own sets, with ≥3 option assets for the Look panel. Submit them to UI Review (review.mjs submit --choices, group 'rebuild-own-token-sets-every-grid-tab - <time>').

Run the full checks (validate --framework, tracker --check, gen-fixtures diff clean, new tests, console typecheck and build). Write the report _claude/builds/reports/rebuild-own-token-sets-every-grid-tab.md, a differences report against the old branch, and the rebuild LOG entry. Add the THREADS row, push the branch, open the PR saying how each feature is reached by deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice and that the UI review is waiting, then link it with builds-live.mjs link.

steps.text: Read the archived branch claude/own-token-sets-for-grids-and-tab-groups for intent only (git log/diff, no merge). Write the design notes for the per-instance look record (instance-look@1): keys rowBg, rowAltBg, textSize, spacing, borderW, borderColor, radius, hoverBg, selectedBg, selectedFg; values are token refs or scaled steps, never raw px or colours; scope key is kind + settings id. Commit the notes to _claude/builds/reports/own-look-per-grid-and-tab-group.md (design section).
steps.why: schema design for a new cross-app look contract

steps.text: Add the instance-look@1 shape to framework/schemas (customize.json style target or a new entry in asset-types.json with a skin declaration), run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs schemas` to regenerate json/, and add validators that refuse raw px or colour values.
steps.why: schema + asset-type registry change shared by every app

steps.text: Reference engine framework/core/engines/instance-look.ts: resolve(skin tokens, app overrides, instance look) → scoped CSS vars (--fx-inst-*) for one grid or tab group, child over parent, an empty record = skin, and reset() drops the record. Pure TS with no DOM code.
steps.why: engine internals: token resolution order over skins

steps.text: Storage keys and migration: per-instance settings keys axf.chrome.tab-group.<id>.look and axf.chrome.grid.<id>.look in the chrome-settings rules. Migrate any legacy per-row overrides into them so nothing is lost. Hook it into skin-coverage so the type counts as covered.
steps.why: settings-key contract + migration across apps

steps.text: Fixtures: add cases to framework/spec/fixtures/instance-look.json (skin only, partial override, full override, reset, skin swap under an override, invalid raw value refused) and generate them with `npx -y tsx framework/spec/gen-fixtures.mts`. Record the Kotlin twin as a deferred gap in framework/spec/PORTING.md (Android is on hold).
steps.why: cross-port conformance contract

steps.text: Make framework/react/components/TabGroup.tsx read its instance look through the engine and set the scoped --fx-inst-* vars on its root. Add matching tab-group rules in framework/ui/axf.css that read only those vars and fall back through the skin cascade, with no var() fallbacks.
Same for the framework grid (DataGrid): row bg, alternating rows, text size, cell spacing, borders, radius, and hover and selected colours from --fx-inst-*. Make sure it keeps fixed cell widths.

Add grid to the right-click chrome block (ChromeContext) so every DataGrid gets Settings… / Change… / Move with a stable settings id (data-axf-grid or the grid id prop). Add the default settings/chrome-grid asset and run `node framework/cli/chrome-settings.mjs backfill` for the per-app copies.

Add a 'Look' section to the chrome-tab-group and chrome-grid settings assets: token pickers for every look key, a live preview on the instance, and a Reset to skin button with confirm and one undo. Use framework controls only and give every control a level-toolbar level.

API part 1: console-control addresses for every instance look (setting:chrome.<kind>.<id>.look.<key>, an action address for reset) registered through control@1 with append-only targets at the end. Add deep links that open an instance's Settings → Look (console_show target).

API part 2: REST routes in the theme-manager plugin: GET/PUT/DELETE /api/plugins/theme-manager/instance-look/<kind>/<id> plus a list route. Expose them as MCP tools through plugin-commands, and add console actions chrome.look.get|set|reset|list for AmberX voice.

API part 3: CLI `node framework/cli/instance-look.mjs get|set|reset|list <kind> <id> [key=value…]` writing the same settings keys through the console API or the hub look document. Wire `axf look …` into axf.mjs and add help text.

Rebake the shared assets and framework into the listed apps (`node framework/cli/shared-assets.mjs bake`, `rebake.mjs apply` for console-web and the others). Run check-theme, check-controls, check-chrome-assets, chrome-settings check and check-console-control, and fix any findings.

Tests: framework/spec/check-instance-look.mts (engine vs fixtures, skin swap restyles, reset returns to the skin), a route test in the theme-manager plugin, and a CLI round-trip. Add them to CI and confirm check-skin-coverage passes.
UI Review: shoot desktop + phone of a grid and a tab group with an own look and with Reset to skin. Submit 3 option looks as assets (review.mjs submit --choices), owner theme-manager.

Wrap-up: run the whole suite (validate --framework, tracker --check, check-instance-look, check-skin-coverage, chrome checks, console typecheck/build). Finish the report _claude/builds/reports/own-look-per-grid-and-tab-group.md, listing how each feature is reached by deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice. Add the THREADS row, push the branch and open the PR for the merge queue.

"They all gotta ship all assets that can be shared bruh!"): no opt-out switch, no look tabs or scopes that draw an app under a look that isn't the hub's, no local fallback. - Skins: every app has its own look (Nov 4 2026, Brett: "by default they're all their own." + "every one has a reset, restore to default."; build `skins`; replaces the "any look change applies to all" part of the rule above, the look still comes from axHub only): each app's slots, spacing and hidden chrome are in its own app-look@1 document on the hub (`shared/settings/looks/<app>.json`), snapshotted as that app's default when skins landed. A skin (skin@1, `framework/assets/skin/`, design packages read as skins too) is a layout + colour + style theme plus assets, switched on per app with Use skin (off by default); a pick with a skin on overrides just that part (Back to skin), and Restore to default puts the app back on its snapshot with a confirm and one undo. Settings → Appearance is the Theme manager in every app: one shared panel, `AppearancePanel` in `framework/libs/settings`. Control@1 token overrides (`axf.tokens.*`) still reach every app. CLI `node framework/cli/skins.mjs`, MCP through the theme-manager routes, CI `npx -y tsx framework/spec/check-skin.mts`. Format built on Opus, possible Fable review: plan `skins-possible-fable-review-6xha`. Spec: `framework/spec/APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md`.
- Skins cover every asset type, at any scope (Nov 7 2026, Brett: "Upgrade the skins system so it styles EVERY asset type now in the registry … Skins apply at any scope: global/app/UI/plugin, with child-overrides-parent inheritance … A skin is a design pack; it MAY reference an icon pack … no hardcoded list; add a CI check that fails if a registered asset type has no skin coverage."; build `skins-asset-types`, Fable): how a skin reaches each asset type is worked out from `framework/schemas/asset-types.json` itself (skin-coverage@1, `framework/core/engines/skin-coverage.mjs`): every type is a slot unless excluded; widgets and attachables are styled through their style target in `schemas/customize.json` (`parts` on the skin: box / text / icon / items); the few types with no look or that are bundles declare `"skin": { "by": slot | parts | reference | bundle | none, via?, why? }` on their registry entry. Every view root and every plugin root is a `<SkinScope>` (framework/react). Parity: Settings → Appearance (Where / What a skin covers), `node framework/cli/skins.mjs use|off|inherit|follow|global|at|coverage|covers`, the theme-manager routes (MCP by plugin-commands), actions `skin.inherit`, `skin.scope`. Report: `_claude/builds/reports/skins-asset-types.md`.

steps.text: Read the archived branch claude/own-token-sets-for-grids-and-tab-groups for intent only (git log/diff, no merge). Write the design notes for the per-instance look record (instance-look@1): keys rowBg, rowAltBg, textSize, spacing, borderW, borderColor, radius, hoverBg, selectedBg, selectedFg; values are token refs or scaled steps, never raw px or colours; scope key is kind + settings id. steps.why: schema design for a new cross-app look contract

steps.text: Add the instance-look@1 shape to framework/schemas (customize.json style target or a new entry in asset-types.json with a skin declaration), run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs schemas` to regenerate json/, and add validators that refuse raw px or colour values.

steps.text: Reference engine framework/core/engines/instance-look.ts: resolve(skin tokens, app overrides, instance look) → scoped CSS vars (--fx-inst-*) for one grid or tab group, child over parent, an empty record = skin, and reset() drops the record. Pure TS with no DOM code.
steps.why: engine internals: token resolution order over skins

steps.text: Storage keys and migration: per-instance settings keys axf.chrome.tab-group.<id>.look and axf.chrome.grid.<id>.look in the chrome-settings rules. Migrate any legacy per-row overrides into them so nothing is lost. Hook it into skin-coverage so the type counts as covered.
steps.why: settings-key contract + migration across apps

steps.text: Fixtures: add cases to framework/spec/fixtures/instance-look.json (skin only, partial override, full override, reset, skin swap under an override, invalid raw value refused) and generate them with `npx -y tsx framework/spec/gen-fixtures.mts`. steps.why: cross-port conformance contract

Same for the framework grid (DataGrid): row bg, alternating rows, text size, cell spacing, borders, radius, and hover and selected colours from --fx-inst-*. Make sure it keeps fixed cell widths.

API part 2: REST routes in the theme-manager plugin: GET/PUT/DELETE /api/plugins/theme-manager/instance-look/<kind>/<id> plus a list route. Expose them as MCP tools through plugin-commands, and add console actions chrome.look.get|set|reset|list for AmberX voice.

API part 3: CLI `node framework/cli/instance-look.mjs get|set|reset|list <kind> <id> [key=value…]` writing the same settings keys through the console API or the hub look document. Wire `axf look …` into axf.mjs and add help text.

Tests: framework/spec/check-instance-look.mts (engine vs fixtures, skin swap restyles, reset returns to the skin), a route test in the theme-manager plugin, and a CLI round-trip. Add them to CI and confirm check-skin-coverage passes.
UI Review: shoot desktop + phone of a grid and a tab group with an own look and with Reset to skin. Submit 3 option looks as assets (review.mjs submit --choices), owner theme-manager.

Wrap-up: run the whole suite (validate --framework, tracker --check, check-instance-look, check-skin-coverage, chrome checks, console typecheck/build). Finish the report _claude/builds/reports/own-look-per-grid-and-tab-group.md, listing how each feature is reached by deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice. Add the THREADS row, push the branch and open the PR for the merge queue.

Finish the report _claude/builds/reports/own-look-per-grid-and-tab-group.md, listing how each feature is reached by deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice. - The look comes from axHub only, and every app ships every shareable asset (Nov 1 2026, Brett: "The apps should only get appearance from axhub period." Control@1 token overrides (`axf.tokens.*`) still reach every app. CLI `node framework/cli/skins.mjs`, MCP through the theme-manager routes, CI `npx -y tsx framework/spec/check-skin.mts`. Format built on Opus, possible Fable review: plan `skins-possible-fable-review-6xha`. Spec: `framework/spec/APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md`.
- Skins cover every asset type, at any scope (Nov 7 2026, Brett: "Upgrade the skins system so it styles EVERY asset type now in the registry … Skins apply at any scope: global/app/UI/plugin, with child-overrides-parent inheritance … A skin is a design pack; it MAY reference an icon pack … no hardcoded list; add a CI check that fails if a registered asset type has no skin coverage."; build `skins-asset-types`, Fable): how a skin reaches each asset type is worked out from `framework/schemas/asset-types.json` itself (skin-coverage@1, `framework/core/engines/skin-coverage.mjs`): every type is a slot unless excluded; widgets and attachables are styled through their style target in `schemas/customize.json` (`parts` on the skin: box / text / icon / items); the few types with no look or that are bundles declare `"skin": { "by": slot | parts | reference | bundle | none, via?, why? }` on their registry entry. Every view root and every plugin root is a `<SkinScope>` (framework/react). Parity: Settings → Appearance (Where / What a skin covers), `node framework/cli/skins.mjs use|off|inherit|follow|global|at|coverage|covers`, the theme-manager routes (MCP by plugin-commands), actions `skin.inherit`, `skin.scope`. Report: `_claude/builds/reports/skins-asset-types.md`.
- Stay in this one session; no sub-agents; keep every step within its cap; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
- Watch live: when you start on a screen or element, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "<what you are changing>"` so the live preview follows you.
- Code, comments, commits, PRs and docs stay clean and professional. In what you say to Brett you are Amber: short, blunt, lead with the result, plain phone-readable lines, say what broke and what it cost.

before.title: Console Android app: thin WebView wrapper with overlay, replaces AmberX
before.detail:
New Android app that replaces AmberX: a thin native shell that runs the AXF console web app in a WebView. Not a native rewrite.
- Native only where Android requires it: draw-over-apps floating toolbar/bubble (port from overlay-toolbar-v2), approvals bar, notifications, mic/recorder, open_url, wake, permissions. Everything else is the web console.
- SAFE AREA (Brett's screenshots, Nov 13): AmberX drew its top bar under the status bar, so the clock, camera cutout, call pill, notification icons and signal sat on top of the title/search/menu. The wrapper must handle WindowInsets (status bar, display cutout, navigation bar, IME), pass them into the WebView as CSS env(safe-area-inset-*) with viewport-fit=cover, and the console must pad every top bar, banner, toolbar and bottom nav with them. Nothing is ever drawn under the clock, camera or notification shade. Test on cutout and punch-hole phones, portrait and landscape.
- The floating toolbar expands to the full-screen console with the toolbar top-left, keeps the app in front, and pops up approvals with a link to the approvals page.
- A JS bridge exposes the native features to the console (window.axfNative), with full API parity: REST/MCP/CLI/voice.
- Auto-updates the web content from the live console. The shell rarely needs a rebuild.
- Migrate AmberX's axHub device service (amberx.open_url, recorder) to the new app.
- Tests, help, Shipped features.

before.title: Auto-land: every finished build lands itself immediately
before.detail:
Brett is sick of finished builds sitting unlanded until they're thousands of commits behind. Make auto-land the DEFAULT for every build (the per-build switch stays, default ON):
- The moment a build finishes and its tests pass, the server lands it on main (build_land logic: push, merge origin/main, union-merge THREADS/STATUS/decisions, settle orchestrator JSON, check JSON, push).
- Lands go through ONE serial landing queue, so two lands never race (fixes 'cannot lock ref origin/main').
- On a code clash or failing test, the server automatically queues a P0 'merge main and land' fix build for it and keeps retrying until it lands. Brett gets an FYI notification for each attempt, not a question.
- A build that's still running gets main merged into its branch every 30 minutes, so it never falls far behind.
- A sweeper runs every 10 minutes: any finished-but-unlanded build is landed or gets its fix build.
- A banner/badge shows the landing queue and anything stuck for over 30 minutes.
- Full API and voice. Tests, help, Shipped features.
